items.title: ‘Once they see the money, they keep building’: Inside Delhi’s PG ecosystem built on a hostel shortage
items.summary: On the first floor of a building in the main market of Satya Niketan is a restaurant. The second floor houses a hotel. The third floor is locked. The fourth floor is a boys’ paying guest accommodation with five rooms, let out on double and triple occupancy. On the fifth, on a terrace lined with garbage and dirt, another room has been built. A telephone tower looms over the structure. For Arnav Yadav, a first-year student at Motilal Nehru College who moved to this PG in Delhi from Firozabad for higher education, the building has become a source of fear. On Sunday, a PG building in the same neighbourhood had collapsed, killing seven. “I am sure this building is illegal too. I am scared this incident can happen anywhere again in Satya Niketan,” he said. The building that came down on Sunday housed Hostel Daze, a boys’ PG. The collapse has since set off the familiar machinery of official response. In an official release, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi said that it has so far identified 1,355 buildings across Delhi where PG facilities are operational, accommodating approximately 27,000 occupants. items.title: CJI Surya Kant proposes register on arbitrators’ conflicts, caseload
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Friday proposed a common cross-institutional register containing details about an arbitrator’s conflicts, existing caseload, average time taken to deliver awards and areas of expertise. The CJI made the suggestion while delivering the keynote address at the closing session of India ADR Week 2026 in New Delhi, which marked ten years of the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA). CJI Kant said arbitrators should be chosen on the basis of publicly available data on their track record rather than reputation circulating within closed legal circles. “ Let Counsel choose Arbitrators the way any serious professional chooses a specialist, based on a visible track record, rather than on reputation transmitted only through closed circles ,” the CJI said. CJI Kant added that arbitral institutions need not wait for a statutory regulator to introduce such transparency. He noted that the law creating the Arbitration Council of India was passed in 2019 but had not yet been notified. “Let transparency do the work that regulation is expected to do. items.title: Corruption in TVK government? | CM Vijay | Shabbir Ahmed | TNM Tamil
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has promised a corruption-free governance as a central promise of his administration. In his first months in office, he has spoken about strengthening vigilance mechanisms, ensuring transparency in government contracts and taking action against officials involved in corruption. But how much of this is translating into change on the ground? Tamil Nadu already has institutions such as the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) to investigate and act on corruption complaints. Yet questions over the independence of these mechanisms, delays in investigations and the role of political and administrative approvals remain. In this week’s episode of Yen Endra Kelvi, Shabbir Ahmed speaks to Jayaram Venkatesh, Convener of Arappor Iyakkam, to examine whether government anti-corruption steps becoming more effective, how officials are responding to the new government’s approach, and discuss about building a system that can sustain the fight against corruption.

items.title: A Fundamental Right
